facts.fact: Neela's first contract (at nineteen) was Raghu, a collector who worked for a Kodiyur port enforcer on the quays behind the pepper warehouses; he had crippled a boatman's eleven-year-old son's arm with a stick. She killed him with a marma strike at the base of the skull in a lane behind the fish market, was sick in a drain, then went back and ate.
facts.why: needed because the outline has her tell the first contract plainly; name, age and method invented.

facts.fact: The first contract leaf carried a small hooked mark in one corner, which Chathu said was for the accounts.
facts.why: clue C15, echoing the 'hook' mark in Ittan's tally book (F448) for later payoff.

facts.fact: Neela and Devan agree the ledger-veto bargain: whoever holds the ledger and begins to read a page at night for any reason, the other takes it from their hand and they let go, no reasons given; each swears it twice. Pages may be read only by daylight, aloud, before the subject.
Neela remembers some of her other contracts: a magistrate with a bad knee, two sisters in a coast house, a boy on a river barge and his buyer.
facts.why: flesh for the 'ten untold' she counts; details are only passing glimpses, not plot.

facts.fact: A small door in the wall beside the warden's chamber hearth, which Neela counts as a door and has found no use for.
